To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose Neural Arithmetic Units (NAUs), a family of components for neural networks that are able to perform exact addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
we introduce two new neural network units for exact arithmetic, the NAU and the NMU, which learn faster than previous units, and can extrapolation to negative and small inputs.
Neural Arithmetic Units can learn exact arithmetic operations, can be trained to be sparse, and can learn for larger hidden sizes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions. Can we build neural network components that can learn to perform exact arithmetic?
the question of whether neural networks can be made more expressive by incorporating inductive biases for arithmetic operations.
the design of neural units that can perform exact arithmetic operations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NAU and the NMU are the most efficient and consistent neural arithmetic units proposed to date.
we propose two new units, which can be plugged into existing neural networks, and which can learn exact arithmetic operations.

our proposed Neural Addition Unit ( NAU ) and Neural Multiplication Unit can learn to perform exact arithmetic operation over real numbers and can learn to extrapolate to negative numbers and small values.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NAU and the NMU can learn to perform arithmetic operations with a small set of parameters, while maintaining the flexibility of neural networks.

neural units can be trained to perform arithmetic operations over real-valued numbers.
